title: Add personal health track records (labs & vitals) to form a baseline health profile

requirements.text: Add backend support for per-user personal health track records so a signed-in user can store and retrieve lab/vitals measurements (including CBC metrics like hemoglobin and platelets, and blood pressure values) as part of their health profile baseline.

quotes: Also, give option for a personal track record type... CBC test... he should be able to put hemoglobin levels, platelet levels and blood pressure, high BP, low BP, everything... so as the health profile... will be used as a median or as a starting point.

acceptanceCriteria: Backend exposes an API to create a health track record entry for the authenticated caller.
Backend exposes an API to list the authenticated caller’s health track record entries (most recent first).
Records are isolated by Internet Identity principal (no user can read/write another user’s records).
At minimum, the backend data model supports these record types: hemoglobin, platelets, blood pressure systolic (high), blood pressure diastolic (low).
Each record stores: record type, numeric value, unit (where applicable), and a date/time or day identifier.
Backend validates that numeric values are non-negative and rejects invalid inputs with a clear error (trap or Result-style error, consistent with existing patterns).

requirements.text: Add backend support for a “baseline snapshot” derived from the user’s track records that can be used as a starting point (e.g., latest value per metric), and expose it via a dedicated query API.

quotes: ...health profile will be formed and will be used as a median or as a starting point.

acceptanceCriteria: Backend exposes a query that returns a baseline snapshot for the caller containing the latest entry per supported metric type (hemoglobin, platelets, BP systolic, BP diastolic).
If no records exist for a metric, that metric is returned as missing/empty (not trapped).
The snapshot query does not require the user profile (height/age/goal) to be present and does not trap due to missing profile fields.

requirements.text: Add a new authenticated UI area for “Health Records” where users can add and view personal track record entries for labs and vitals, using English user-facing text.

quotes: Also, give option for a personal track record type... he should be able to put hemoglobin levels, platelet levels and blood pressure, high BP, low BP, everything...

acceptanceCriteria: App includes a reachable Health Records page or section while logged in.
The UI provides an “Add Record” form that supports: Hemoglobin, Platelets, Blood Pressure (High/Systolic), Blood Pressure (Low/Diastolic).
The form collects value and date (and unit if not implied) and prevents submission with invalid/empty values, showing an English validation message.
After saving, the new record appears in the records list without requiring a full page refresh (React Query invalidation/refetch pattern).
The records list shows type, value + unit, and date, sorted newest-first.

requirements.text: Add navigation entry points so users can easily find and use Health Records from the existing logged-in experience (without disrupting existing dashboard, logging, scanning, chat, or install flows).
acceptanceCriteria: There is a visible navigation entry point to Health Records from the logged-in UI (e.g., header nav and/or dashboard quick action).
Navigation uses the existing TanStack Router route setup pattern in frontend/src/App.tsx.
All user-facing labels for the new navigation item and page are in English.

requirements.text: Display the caller’s baseline health snapshot (latest hemoglobin/platelets/BP high/BP low when available) in a compact, read-only summary card so the user can see their starting point at a glance.

quotes: ...health profile will be formed and will be used as a median or as a starting point.

acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard (or another consistently visible logged-in location) shows a compact “Baseline Health” summary when at least one record exists.
The summary displays the latest available value for each metric type; missing metrics are either omitted or shown as “Not set” (English).
If the snapshot query fails, the UI degrades gracefully (no app crash) and shows a small English fallback message (e.g., “Could not load baseline health data”).

constraints: Use English for any user-facing text.
Backend must remain a single Motoko actor in backend/main.mo (no additional backend services).
Do not edit files under frontend/src/components/ui (compose existing UI components instead).
Preserve per-principal data isolation using the existing access control checks/patterns.
Do not introduce any external APIs or external databases for storing health records.
nonGoals: No medical diagnosis, recommendations, or risk scoring based on lab/vitals values.
No external lab integrations, file uploads, or PDF parsing for test reports.
No real-time syncing or notifications for health record updates.
No changes to Internet Identity authentication flow.
No changes to existing BMI/TDEE calculation logic beyond adding the new baseline snapshot feature.
